newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia says it would back Paris five-power summit.
newsitem.headline: Russia says it would back Paris five-power summit.

text.p: Russia declared on Thursday it was ready to take part in a five-power summit which it said had been mooted by Western leaders to discuss future European security.
U.S. officials said they had not promoted such an idea.

Kremlin spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky, quoted by Interfax news agency, confirmed media reports that the meeting, ahead of a NATO summit that will decide on alliance eastward expansion, had been discussed between Russia and NATO leaders.

Diplomats in Paris said French President Jacques Chirac, encouraged by a weekend meeting with Boris Yeltsin, had floated the idea of a summit to include Russia, France, the United States, Germany and Britain.
The meeting would discuss Kremlin concerns over NATO plans to absorb former Russian Warsaw Pact allies, which Russian leaders see as undermining their authority and threatening security.
An alliance summit in Madrid this summer is expected to issue the first invitations.
"Indeed the question of a meeting of the "Big Five" this spring arose at meetings in Moscow," Yastrzhembsky said.

"The main thing for us is the question of the content of this meeting and of its careful preparation. As a result of the meeting we would have to find our way to a realistic result that would suit everyone," he added.
But in Washington, State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns, asked about the suggestion, said: "We have not received any such proposal from the French government.
U.S. officials, speaking on condition they were not identified said they had certainly not encouraged any such idea.
